$doc: Curated language-support extensions shipped as built-ins.
This file is the source of truth; product.json's builtInExtensions entries for these are GENERATED.
Run `npm run sync-language-extensions` after editing, which resolves versions against Open VSX,
downloads each vsix, records its sha256, and rewrites the managed block in product.json.
Never hand-edit a generated entry -- it will be overwritten and the sha256 will be wrong.
name        publisher.extension, exactly as Open VSX namespaces it
language    what this exists to support; for the docs and the coverage report
license     the license you VERIFIED, not the one the API claims; the sync fails if they disagree
repo        upstream source, recorded in product.json for the attribution manifest
version     optional hard pin. Omit to track the newest stable release
allowPreRelease  set only when upstream publishes NOTHING but pre-releases to Open VSX
serverDelivery   bundled | download | external -- 'bundled' is the only air-gap-safe value
notes       why this pick, or what is compromised about it

extensions.name: cosven.easy-groovy
extensions.notes: The only Groovy extension on Open VSX that bundles a language server. GroovyLanguageServer.groovy-language-server does not exist there.

extensions.name: crystal-lang-tools.crystal-lang
extensions.notes: Requires crystalline or scry on PATH.

extensions.name: denoland.vscode-deno
extensions.notes: Uses `deno lsp` from the installed Deno binary. Inert without it.

extensions.name: detachhead.basedpyright
extensions.notes: Pyright fork, MIT with Microsoft's copyright retained. Carries dist/server.js plus typeshed-fallback and zero native binaries, so it runs on the editor's own Node. Registers callHierarchy but not typeHierarchy. Vendored licenses: extension/dist/typeshed-fallback/LICENSE, extracted and read -- Apache-2.0 for typeshed itself with some MIT stubs noted in its appendix, no copyleft; the file ships inside the vsix so its notice travels with the binary. Needs two defaults set in the fork: basedpyright.importStrategy = useBundled (the default reads ms-python.python's API and throws when absent) and python.languageServer = None (otherwise it opens a modal on first Python file).

extensions.name: erlang-ls.erlang-ls
extensions.notes: erlang_ls and els_dap binaries ship inside the vsix. STALE: 0.0.39 dates from 2022-10 and is the only published version.

extensions.name: gleam.gleam
extensions.notes: Open VSX license field is null; Apache-2.0 established from the packaged LICENSE and the repo. Uses `gleam lsp` from the installed toolchain.

extensions.name: GraphQL.vscode-graphql
extensions.notes: Hard extensionDependency on GraphQL.vscode-graphql-syntax, which is shipped alongside. Do not pin the newest version: 0.13.6-alpha.0 is published with preRelease=false despite the semver tag.

extensions.name: GraphQL.vscode-graphql-syntax
extensions.notes: Grammar only. Present solely because GraphQL.vscode-graphql declares it as a hard extensionDependency and will not activate without it.

extensions.name: Ionide.Ionide-fsharp
extensions.notes: FsAutoComplete ships complete in the vsix (~53 MB: fsautocomplete.dll, FSharp.Compiler.Service, Roslyn, plus native SQLite for every OS, which is why one universal package covers all platforms). Server is Apache-2.0, bundled Roslyn/FCS are MIT. Framework-dependent, not self-contained: needs a .NET 8/9 runtime on the machine. CAVEAT: the published manifest has extensionPack listing muhammad-sammy.csharp (non-redistributable, see notes there) and anysphere.csharp (absent from Open VSX). extensionPack members are recommendations, not hard dependencies, so F# works without them and nothing non-redistributable is shipped -- but the recommendation is visible to users.

extensions.name: jnoortheen.nix-ide
extensions.notes: Requires nixd or nil on PATH.

extensions.name: julialang.language-julia
extensions.notes: LanguageServer.jl ships in the vsix, but needs a Julia runtime on the machine to execute.

extensions.name: mads-hartmann.bash-ide-vscode
extensions.notes: bash-language-server bundled as JS. Shellcheck integration is optional and degrades to no-op when absent.

extensions.name: ms-vscode.powershell
extensions.notes: PowerShell Editor Services bundled. Open VSX metadata says "SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.txt"; the packaged text is verbatim MIT, (c) Microsoft.

extensions.name: mshr-h.veriloghdl
extensions.notes: Open VSX license field is absent (upstream package.json carries none); MIT established from the packaged LICENSE.txt and the repo. Requires an external HDL language server such as svls or veridian.

extensions.name: NomicFoundation.hardhat-solidity
extensions.notes: Language server fully bundled including slang WASM and prebuilt solidity-analyzer. Chosen over JuanBlanco.solidity, which vendors 499 third-party licenses with several needing manual review.

extensions.name: redhat.java
extensions.notes: Eclipse JDT.LS ships inside the vsix (~54 MB of OSGi jars, universal, with equinox launchers for every platform). EPL-2.0 source offer is discharged by the repo URL in the notices file, since we redistribute unmodified. Red Hat publishes only CI builds to Open VSX, hence allowPreRelease. NOTE: no JRE is bundled -- the machine needs a JDK, resolved via java.jdt.ls.java.home / JAVA_HOME / the Windows registry.

extensions.name: redhat.vscode-yaml
extensions.notes: yaml-language-server ships inside the vsix as JS; no native binary, no runtime download.
